big: Rohan's car is damaged on a Friday night. He is tempted to repair it first and tell the insurer later. If he does, the insurer may refuse, since it was never allowed to see the damage.

lines: What is the right order of steps when I need to claim?
Tell the insurer at once, keep the damage as it is for the surveyor, send the documents asked for, and read the exclusions beforehand so no claim surprises you.

rows: Inform the insurer promptly, within the time the policy allows
A licensed surveyor inspects and assesses the loss
Send the forms, bills and proofs asked for
The insurer pays, or explains any exclusion that applies
note: An exclusion is a situation the policy does not cover. Read the list when you buy, not after the loss.

title: Making a claim
stops: Inform the insurer promptly after a loss
Repair first and inform later is always fine
A surveyor is appointed to assess the loss
Exclusions can be ignored at claim time
caps: Delay can lead to a refused claim, so intimate within the time allowed.
If the damage is repaired first, the insurer cannot assess it.
A licensed surveyor inspects and reports the extent of the loss.
Exclusions are not covered, so read them when you buy.

q: Meena's vehicle is damaged in an accident. What should she do first?
opts: Repair it first and tell them later
Wait for the insurer to call her
Sell the vehicle as it is
why: Repairing first stops the insurer from assessing the damage.
The insurer cannot act until it is informed, so waiting for a call is risky.
Selling the vehicle is not needed and can complicate the claim.
Claim intimation within the allowed time keeps her claim valid.

q: Who is the surveyor in a claim?
opts: A licensed person the insurer appoints
A person selected by the repair shop
why: A surveyor is licensed and is appointed by the insurer.
A friend has no licence or role in assessing a loss.
A repair shop's person would not be an independent assessor.
A newspaper person has no role in a claim at all.

q: Rohan's claim is for a cause that the policy lists as an exclusion. What is likely?
opts: The insurer pays double the amount
The sum insured is raised at once
The insurer may not pay for that cause
why: Insurers do not pay extra for an excluded cause.
A claim does not raise the sum insured on any basis.
An exclusion is a situation the policy does not cover.
Exclusions stay in force, and are not cancelled by a claim.

q: Meena buys a new policy and finds that the terms differ from what she was told. What can she do?
opts: Do nothing, since the money is paid
Use the review window to return it
Wait until a claim and then complain
Tear up the papers and forget them
why: Paying does not take away her right to review it.
A short review window lets her return it for a refund, under terms.
Waiting until a claim is too late, as the window is short.
Tearing up the papers loses the proof she needs.

pts: Tell the insurer promptly. Do not repair before the survey.
A surveyor assesses the loss. Send every document asked for.
Read the exclusions when you buy, not after the loss.
